title: The Slow Bakery
premise: Silas Whitlock has spent eleven years keeping his heart as orderly as his bookshop, raising his daughter alone after the woman he loved left town to honor a family obligation. When a renovation tears open a wall and reveals a letter he never received — her confession of love, postmarked the week she left — Silas tracks down Ada Okafor, now a powerful bakery executive engaged to a man who secured her rise. As Ada returns to reopen the town's shuttered bakery, old love collides with duty, ambition, and the machinery of power that corrupted everything she built. In the end, Ada must choose: she walks away from the merger that would have made her, stays past the last train on the night of the bakery's reopening, and chooses Silas — not as an escape from her life, but as the first honest thing in it.
about_author: Cyrus Oyelaran is a former small-town bookseller who writes romances about people who mistake discipline for peace. He lives near a railway line and insists the last train is the most romantic sound in the world.

chapters.title: The Wall Gives Up Its Secret
chapters.summary: Silas's POV. Renovating the bookshop's back room, Silas and his daughter June pry loose a brick and find a yellowed letter addressed to him, postmarked eleven years ago. He reads Ada's confession alone at closing time and realizes his whole careful life was built on a silence he never questioned. The beat is quiet devastation — grief arriving late, with interest.

chapters.title: What Power Buys
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. Now a rising executive, Ada returns to Hollow Creek to oversee the acquisition and demolition of the town's old bakery — a deal her fiancé Marcus engineered using her name. Seeing Silas across the square reopens everything; learning he never got her letter teaches her that Marcus intercepted it years ago. The beat is fury curdling into clarity about how thoroughly her ambition was weaponized against her.

chapters.title: Closing Time Arguments
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Over three nights in the bookshop, Silas and Ada argue their way through eleven years — duty, resentment, June, the letter, the deal. Ada discovers the merger requires demolishing the bakery block including Silas's shop, forcing her to choose between the future Marcus built for her and the town she abandoned. The beat is rising tension: love reigniting exactly as it becomes unaffordable.

chapters.title: After the Last Train
chapters.summary: Ada's POV, then shared. At the merger signing, Ada publicly withdraws, torching her career and engagement to save the bakery block. She races the last train to Hollow Creek, finds Silas locking up, and instead of boarding, asks to stay. Epilogue-tinged final scene: months later, the bakery reopens next door to the bookshop, flour dusting the paperbacks. The beat is resolution — love chosen freely, not owed.
